alignment_note: TV009 has two unequal nausea outputs with identical evidence. The unchanged evaluator refuses to choose the scored one, counting one unmatched reference and two extra outputs. Together with TV007 this gives 14 matched, 3 extra, 1 missing, despite only two excess raw records.
severity_assessment: Localized but meaningful data-quality defect: duplicate detail records and ambiguous matching. Current daily severity aggregation ignores null severity, so these empty-score duplicates do not increase the known daily rating. Existing dashboard inputs were not replaced.
offline_replay: Replaying all ten saved candidate batches with the unchanged normalizer reproduced every saved normalized output. No API calls or repairs.
whole_report_rule: Successful processing; no missing/extra observations or candidates; all candidate checks and normalized core fields correct; issue flags match; all quotes exact and complete. Exact time_text differences reported separately and reviewed for semantic validity.
interpretation: Targeted vomiting grouping, contiguous copying, and nausea scope recover. Two nausea duplicate groups remain; whole-report pass is 8/10, improving over the long grouping run and tying the earlier evidence run with different failures.
limitations: The ten examples are known synthetic development/regression data; not fresh validation or independent human clinical annotation.
Text generator and extractor share a model family; wording is controlled and repetitive.
One new attempt per report against saved single attempts; no stability estimate or causal isolation of shortening.
This is a combined change in length, specificity, and copying instructions; improvement cannot be attributed to length alone.
No distinct-date/window/event/medication negative controls here; no broad overmerge-safety claim.
A better result here does not alone justify replacing the default or deploying to the dashboard.
